analyst.summary: IRCTC's Q4FY26 print captured the central tension well: revenue hit an all-time high (Rs 1,459.72 crore, +15.1% YoY) while PAT fell 8.9% YoY as consolidated EBIT margin continued a four-year structural slide (36% to 27%) driven by a genuine mix shift toward lower-margin Catering and Tourism, away from the 76%-EBITDA-margin Internet Ticketing core. FY26 full-year PAT grew just 6% against 11.7% revenue growth - negative operating leverage for a second straight year. The stock has already de-rated roughly 80% from its 2020 multiple peak (~169x to ~29-31x trailing versus a ~63x ten-year average), and the perennial convenience-fee/policy overhang (proven real via the 2021 fee-sharing episode that cost the stock ~25% in a day, and freshly relevant via 2026's RTI disclosure and forced website revamp) remains a genuine, recurring tail risk rather than a one-off. Growth optionality - Tourism/Bharat Gaurav, Vande Bharat ramp-up, Rail Neer expansion, a pending payment-aggregator license - is real but not yet large enough to offset the margin drag. Hold: quality and balance-sheet strength are not in question and the multiple has already absorbed much of the bad news, but the structural margin compression is the live variable to watch before the next quarterly print, not a name to add to on quality alone.
